chunks.text:
Hi Tommy,

You're one of the reasons I'm still in Toronto. Some people anchor you to a place, make it feel like somewhere instead of anywhere. You've been a real gravitational pull, the "this place contains someone I care about, so the place matters" kind.

Last year I wrote about how we crossed paths, how you became "Tommy from Twitter" and then just Tommy, how that first walk-and-talk had a clarity to it that made everything else fall into place. This year I'm writing about what happens after that: the workshop, and New Stadium. We've logged a lot of hours now. Dinners, events, late-night conversations, the ambient awareness of each other's lives. The initial spark has settled into something steadier. I think that's better.



```quotes
A true friend is one who is, as it were, a second self.

Cicero, _De Amicitia_ 80
```

Cicero's line sounds grandiose, but I think he just meant the people who know you well enough that you can think out loud with them, who you trust to see your unfinished thoughts, who you don't have to perform for. That's what we have. I can say the half-formed thing and you'll help me figure out what I mean.

---

I'm proud of what [New Systems](/posts/new) achieved this year. The outputs matter, sure, but what I respect more is that you keep making something exist where there could've been excuses instead. You keep pushing things over the line when most people would've found a reason to stop.

Watching you build is one of the cleanest "yes, this is possible" signals in my life. When I wonder if the weird thing I'm working on is worth pursuing, I think about you. You're proof that you can just... do the thing. Make the event. Ship the podcast. Build the community.

---

The laughter thread from 24 still holds. You laugh freely, at yourself, at the absurdity of things, at the small disasters that would make other people tense up. It's permission to not take everything so seriously, to let the stumbles be funny instead of catastrophic.



You made me feel at home in Canada. That's not a small thing. I moved here as a teenager, spent years feeling like a guest in a country that wasn't quite mine. You're one of the people who made Toronto feel like it belongs to me, or like I belong to it. You gave me a sense of place by being a person worth staying for.

---

As always: love you like a distant brother. I'm your biggest fan. If there are none, I'm still your biggest fan. That line from last year hasn't changed, and it won't.

I want 2026 to be full of bangers for you, for New Systems, for all the weird plans that only become real because you keep pushing them over the line.

See you soon.

[^sign]
